question_text: If the equations x² + bx + c = 0 and x² + cx + b = 0 have a common root, then show that b + c + 1 = 0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — say what you do with the two equations to find the common root, and where you put that root afterwards.
insider_note: Subtract the two equations so α² cancels: (b − c)(α − 1) = 0 forces α = 1 when b ≠ c. The required line is then one substitution back — stopping at α = 1 leaves the asked result unwritten.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Subtract to find α
steps.margin_note: First mark. Neither equation can be solved on its own, so write both with the common root α and SUBTRACT: the α² terms cancel and (b − c)α + (c − b) = 0, i.e. (b − c)(α − 1) = 0. With b ≠ c, α = 1.
steps.memory_tip: SUBTRACT the two equations so α² cancels: (b − c)(α − 1) = 0, and b ≠ c gives α = 1.
lines: Let α be the common root. Then

recall.must_convey: That α is put into both equations, the two are subtracted so α² cancels, leaving (b − c)(α − 1) = 0, and since b ≠ c the common root is α = 1.
accept: write alpha in both equations and subtract, alpha squared cancels and b minus c into alpha minus one is zero so alpha is one
subtracting the two equations gives the common root alpha equals one
the difference of the two equations factorises as b minus c times alpha minus one
rendu equations subtract cheste alpha square cancel, b minus c into alpha minus one zero, so alpha one
since b is not equal to c the common root must be one

steps.why: Neither equation has numbers in it, so neither can be solved alone; subtracting removes the α² and leaves a linear relation, which is the only way to fix the common root.
common_mistakes: Adding the equations instead of subtracting, which keeps the α² term.
Writing the difference as (b − c)α + (b − c) and getting α = −1.
Dividing by (b − c) without saying b ≠ c.

steps.label: Substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put α = 1 back into either equation: 1 + b + c = 0, which is the required result. One line, but it is the line the question asks for — write it.
steps.memory_tip: Put α = 1 back into either equation: 1 + b + c = 0. That one line is the asked result.

recall.must_convey: That α = 1 is substituted back into one of the equations to give 1 + b + c = 0, which is the statement to be shown.
accept: put alpha equals one into the first equation to get one plus b plus c equals zero hence shown
substitute the common root one back and b plus c plus one is zero
with alpha one, one squared plus b plus c is zero which is the result
alpha one ni first equation lo pettithe one plus b plus c zero, hence shown
b plus c plus one equals zero

steps.why: α = 1 was derived from both equations together, so it satisfies each; substituting into either one turns the root into the relation between b and c that was asked for.
common_mistakes: Stopping at α = 1 and never substituting.
Writing 1 + b + c = 0 as b + c = 1.
